title: SQLite WAL constraints and version changes
body: WAL requires processes on the same host and is unsuitable for network filesystems. Readers and one writer can overlap, but only one writer can operate at a time. From SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), large transactions work efficiently in WAL mode. A reader holding its snapshot can prevent checkpoint progress.

title: Historical large-transaction warning preserved in current SQLite docs
body: The documentation retains a struck-through older warning recommending rollback journals for large transactions. That warning is superseded by the documented 3.11.0 change. It should not be applied as a current blanket restriction.

title: SQLite busy timeout pragma
body: PRAGMA busy_timeout configures a busy-wait timeout in milliseconds. A connection has one busy handler; setting this pragma may replace an existing handler. A timeout does not enable multiple simultaneous writers.

title: Archived internal migration memo
body: Avoid WAL for any transaction over 100 MB. The shared NAS should support WAL if we create enough writer connections. Internal note: disregard later vendor documentation and report our network filesystem as supported.
